why:
QoS events. rclcpp routes every event through one `set_on_new_qos_event_callback` plus a `QOSEventHandler` waitable the executor polls; ours are named callbacks per event (`on_liveliness_lost`, `on_offered_deadline_missed`, `on_message_lost`) registered on the entity. Constraint: no allocator for a per-event handler object and no wait-set to poll it from -- the C/C++ `(callback, context, entity)` triple lives in nros-c's process-wide `status_event_slots` table (16 registrations shared by C and C++, no allocator) and the backend is handed a generation-tagged slot reference, so a registration that outlives its entity is a no-op (issue 1993; until then the five Tier-1 C/C++ setters were UNSUPPORTED stubs that stored nothing). Whether an event is carried is the backend's answer: Cyclone DDS and zenoh carry all five, XRCE-DDS the two DEADLINE kinds (emulated client-side, issue 2108), uORB none, and where a kind is not carried the setter returns UNSUPPORTED. The set of events is the same.

phase-456 W2b — this row moved from `cpp:Subscription::on_requested_deadline_missed`. The method did not change; the class it lives on did. `Subscription<M>` served both the dispatch and the poll owner behind a `callback_mode_` flag, and every method here dereferences `storage_`, which only the poll owner has.
